messages:
marie: Heads up — after we published the exports map change, a customer’s Next.js Edge sample started failing to import the SDK in the edge runtime. stack traces point at a CJS file being pulled into an ESM-only context.

ajay: can you paste the failing import + node/npm/yarn versions?

marie: Import is `import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference-sdk'` inside a Next 13 edge function. Node 18.16, Next using Turbopack. Error: SyntaxError: Cannot use 'require' in ES module — points to dist/index.cjs.

kevin: we did change the exports last week — what did we publish exactly?

marie: we simplified the exports to a wildcard to reduce maintenance: "exports": { "./*": "./dist/*" } and also switched package.json to "type": "module". Locally everything looked fine but the sample (pnpm + hoisted symlinks) resolved to the CJS file in some environments. I have a tiny repro.

sophia: can you paste the relevant package.json snippet so we can see the exact mapping?

marie: ```json
{
  "name": "@redwood/inference-sdk",
  "version": "1.3.0",
  "type": "module",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
    },
    "./utils": "./dist/utils.js"
  },
  "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
}
```

luca: that looks standard. Why would Next/Turbopack pick the CJS entry? Could be pnpm hoisting/symlink resolver or a dependant that imports a subpath.

ajay: also remember some bundlers fall back to `main` or `module` fields if exports doesn't resolve due to package manager quirks. Do we publish `main` or `module` currently?

marie: we removed `main`/`module` when we switched to exports-only. That might be the trigger for older resolvers.

kevin: quick workaround for affected customers: pin to v1.2.3 (before the exports change) or import the ESM file directly `import '@redwood/inference-sdk/dist/index.mjs'` in the edge function. Not great, but unblocks them.

ajay: for a short-term fix we can republish a patch that adds explicit `main` and `module` fields back and ensure `types` is set. Something like: "main": "./dist/index.cjs", "module": "./dist/index.mjs", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts". Also consider reverting the wildcard until we understand the pnpm case.

marie: I opened a quick PR that reverts the wildcard exports and restores dual entry fields + adds a failing sample to CI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/456. Repro is in `dev-samples/edge-sdk-exports-repro` (pnpm + Next + edge fn).

sophia: long-term: publish a dual-directory layout ("cjs/" and "esm/") and use a conditional exports map with explicit `import`/`require`/`types` entries. Add tests that install with npm/yarn/pnpm and run a Next edge build to catch resolver oddities.

luca: also add an entry in the changelog and ping support to proactively reach out to known customers who upgraded last week.

build-bot: CI run for sample test triggered -> `yarn build` failed with the ESM/CJS resolve error.

ajay: assign to eng-devex to add matrixed package resolution tests (pnpm/npm/yarn x next-edge).

marie: will take it. tl;dr: exports map tweak caused surprising consumer resolution behavior in hoisted/pnpm environments which surfaced in Edge runtimes — immediate action: revert/publish patch; medium: expand export map, restore legacy fields, add CI coverage and a sample repro.
